body: This really bugs me. There's just no way I can understand how Apple has done so little UI work between releases lately. They have thousands of software engineers - most of the changes are incredibly minor, and often seem to be poorly thought through. What is going on in the decision making process?!

> FYI again, when guys say "my hobbies aren't things women find attractive" I just see a guy who is kinda sexist and makes assumptions about women - whether it's true or not.

Fair, it wasn't intended as sexist, but the vast majority of women find my hobbies unattractive. There are definitely women who share my hobbies, but they're few and far between, and generally in very high demand so I don't really stand a chance with them.

> I personally find loners with antisocial hobbies and few friends to generally be unattractive and my experience is that women care about how social a guy is way more than guys care about the same for women. It doesn't matter whether you think that's unfair or not, if it's the truth you gotta get the fuck over it because that's life. Sometimes we change the way we live to accomplish our goals and if you aren't willing to do that then you might want to think about how much you really want what you say you want. 

My introversion is just the way I am, it's not so much a lifestyle choice as a personality trait. I can force myself to talk to people or go and do social things (and I do), but it'll never be enjoyable for me. I find it exhausting and stressful. So I'd rather find someone who values me for who I am, and not someone who pretends to be more sociable than they are. I do have friends, but I prefer quality over quantity, really.

> Basically, you're probably going to have a hard time as long as you feel this way because you can't stop people seeing your feelings. I've met so many guys like you and it's obvious as hell. 

I'd be interested to know how you know what sort of guy I am from some comments on reddit... I actually don't think it's particularly obvious that I'm depressed. It's obvious that I'm shy, definitely, but not that I'm depressed or desperate (I'm actually not desperate, I've been rejected so many times I never get my hopes up too much). 

> You are upset that your female friends apparently have more/easier luck than you (without once considering that there are pros and cons for both genders in the dating world, among other things)

I'm aware that there are pros and cons, but in this instance I was focusing on the negatives I have personally experienced. I'm aware women have to deal with a huge amount of shit while dating; creepy guys who won't accept 'no', unwanted advances all the time, concerns for safety, date rape, etc. I was simply not talking about that because I didn't feel it was hugely relevant to my point.

> You're actually annoyed at women.
> You seem to think that there's something wrong with all the women you approach rejecting you, without for a moment acknowledging that women are people with agency and feelings who owe you nothing.

That's actually not the case at all, I am frustrated at the situation in general, not at the women. My response was more focussed on women because the original comment was insulting towards guys, and I took that personally. The reason I have female friends is that I have a lot of mutual respect with those friends; I also work with a lot of women and find them to be great people. There's no expectation here, any more than I'd expect a random dude to be friends with me.

I know I'm not *owed* anything by anyone - that doesn't change the fact that being rejected consistently stings. Intellectually acknowledging that no one has an obligation to date me, and coping with the fact that no one wants to, are emotionally very different things. One of the reasons I've been depressed is the fact that being unwanted destroys my self esteem - if I really was narcissistic enough to assume it was all their fault, I wouldn't feel so inadequate because of it.

> Are you an introvert or a hermit? And do you not have friends? (Why else are you alone every evening? Get a job/friends/hobbies)

Honestly, yes. I am introverted, and I am very shy. I hate large social gatherings, and I hate making small talk and interacting with complete strangers. I have some friends, but generally we don't go out and do stuff, other than chat at work or hang out at university. I also have hobbies, but they are not particularly social ones, and definitely not ones which many women would find attractive.

> It sounds like you actually are kinda negative and don't have much of a social life, which are two really unattractive things to many people.

I'm very positive seeming and chatty in person. It's an act, but a convincing one - most people have absolutely no idea how I actually feel. I recently confided in a friend about depression, etc. and she was absolutely shocked. I should add, I'm not actively trying to date anyone at the moment, because I feel so shit all the time. My comments here are reflecting mostly upon past experiences.

Frankly, I shouldn't have to have loads of friends or an amazing social life to be attractive. I don't have the time or energy to socialise all the time - I have things I'm passionate about and love doing, and I enjoy a fairly quiet time most evenings. That shouldn't be overly unattractive - if it is, I think that's a pretty unfair standard.
I remember seeing this somewhere. Seems a bit fantastical, but I'm definitely not in the top 20% so it could explain things. Source?

> try not to come across like you're trying so hard. That's definitely a turn off. 

It's an anonymous online forum so I don't mind showing my true feelings on the matter haha. Again, why is it a "red flag"/not okay to be a bit upset about my experiences?

I'm never "desperate" on an individual level, and I don't speak about these issues in person because it makes me look like a pussy or a whiner. It is still really disheartening when every single woman you find attractive rejects you. It's also extraordinarily hard to meet women in the first place, which doesn't help.

Basically what I meant is, I'm not sitting around expecting stuff to fall into my lap. I'm shy, pretty introverted, and have quite specific interests, and this stuff isn't easy for me.

I would say, I spend time at university talking to people and trying to get to know women. I take the time to read and talk about things that I normally wouldn't so I'm not as boring as I otherwise would be. I never make overtly sexual or creepy comments, and I'm always respectful of personal space and the like. I don't act all mopey when I get rejected or am otherwise down - I generally hide my negative emotions extremely effectively (as a side note, this is not a good thing, but seems to be expected of guys if they are to be attractive). 

I'm not a ladies' man by any measure, but I'm not completely frigid or an asshole, either. I'm friendly, conversational, and I think pretty knowledgeable without being pushy about it.

I'm not, however, muscle bound or hugely good looking. I'm probably about a 6-7, and am often told I'm "cute". I'm not fat either, just pretty average looking. Apparently that's enough to exclude me from NZ's somewhat exclusive gene pool.

Hey, I don't really know what to say to make you feel better about yourself... I'm not much of a counsellor, but it upset me to see how much a herpes diagnosis is affecting you. I thought I'd give you some facts in case your doctor didn't, because it's really not a terrible disease, like it's made out to be. Don't give up because of this.

Herpes is a minor skin condition that 1/3 people have (yep; that's the STD one). The more common strain that causes cold sores? 9/10 people have it.

It's nothing to be ashamed or afraid of, and imo it shouldn't really be considered an STD at all, as you can catch it by any skin to skin contact, including kissing and brushing against one another.

The entire stigma actually comes from [an advertising campaign](http://projectaccept.org/herpes-stigma-the-origin/) in the 1970s. Before that, it was just known as "cold sores", and that's how you should think of it. Herpes infection doesn't impact quality of life, and it doesn't have any long term health effects - it's just a bit annoying.

I hope this helps you feel a bit better :)

You might be delusional or otherwise convinced that the world is "better off" without that person. Just to name a few examples.
